answer: One defense is a stake-bonded identity registry. Before trading, each agent locks a refundable bond and proves sustained useful work. The registry publishes that history openly, acting as a lantern exposing new identities with no track record. An attacker must pay a bond for every fake agent, and any identity caught spamming or double-signing loses its bond. Old credentials cannot be reused as a relic of past behavior, because endorsements expire and need fresh work. The bond is a ledge: below it no trading allowed, so a Sybil swarm grows linearly expensive while honest agents pay once.
